correctness.rationale: Uniform multiplicative return separation follows from two distinct coordinates. The sup c0 bound is exactly matched by geometrically supported vectors with amplitudes approaching the strict first-coordinate lower threshold. Finite-p geometric-series tails give the lower bracket and the two brackets squeeze the small-ball limit. The disjoint-block series proves dense weighted universality, and a finite-support preimage perturbation proves topological mixing. Strict inequalities, c0 convergence, and p=1 endpoints were checked analytically and sample constructions numerically.

value.rationale: The sharp c0 logarithmic recurrence coefficient quantifies an extremal return-time invariant at every ball radius; the common small-target coefficient on every ell-p gives a natural universal scaling law beyond known qualitative no-frequency results. It provides constructive upper and lower logarithmic packing and exhibits topologically mixing weighted orbit families whose individual returns are nevertheless uniformly sparse. No wider claim of arbitrary weights or shift classification is made.
